evidence.title: install
evidence.finding: Linux, universal macOS and Windows installers, tmux/psmux requirements and manual update/uninstall instructions. Its Claude-only statement is older than the driver implementation.

evidence.title: agents
evidence.finding: Distinct chat, terminal, orchestration, permissions and resume support per harness; generic hook reports cannot approve tools.

evidence.title: board-doc
evidence.finding: Editable lanes compose agent, session or command steps; manual advancement is default, account/model attempts are retained, and orchestrator chat delegates linked card sessions.

evidence.title: memory-doc
evidence.finding: Opt-in project learning, dated file/card sources, human-approved proposals, freshness rechecks and read-only project agent restrictions.

evidence.title: schedule-doc
evidence.finding: Human-created reminders and routines; local minute timer, assistant heartbeat and Telegram replies. Routines report CI/review state and do not independently launch coding work.

evidence.title: architecture
evidence.finding: Local Rust/Tauri/React system, SSH host sessions, Noise relay, encrypted personal sync versus server-readable online board, and inactive Plus billing switch.

evidence.title: release
evidence.finding: 0.1.53 dated 2026-11-19 adds SSH hosts, explicit post-crash resume, external Devflow >=0.5 and security target confirmation.

evidence.title: drivers
evidence.finding: Claude, Codex and ACP drivers are wired into chats; harness support differs from shell-only launches. Driver metadata preserves unavailable cost/context rather than inventing values.

evidence.title: api
evidence.finding: Local stdio MCP and devpit agent CLI expose board/card read/write, comments, sessions, artifact and Devflow operations. Remote MCP has a separate read-only allowlist.

evidence.title: cards
evidence.finding: SQLite cards retain IDs, text, lane, order, due dates, comments and attachments separately from runs. Local comments distinguish person and agent authors and support edit/delete.

evidence.title: edges
evidence.finding: Transactional card/parent/blocker creation rejects cyclic and cross-project waits; board computes readiness, epic progress and cut/superseded release conditions.

evidence.title: plans
evidence.finding: Plans preview child cards and dependencies, wait for human approval, and apply only the last shown plan. Edits, cuts and merges preserve card references.

evidence.title: memory
evidence.locator: seed; propose_or_accept; decide; stale file recheck; project_memory_view.rs
evidence.finding: File-backed facts, lessons and decisions have dates and sources. New repository-only onboarding facts may be accepted automatically with an undo; other proposals await approval. This qualifies older prose saying every memory change waits.

evidence.title: dispatch
evidence.finding: Card play refuses a running step, asks before irreversible steps and creates/reuses card checkout. Optional one-card relay selects unblocked epic children and context handoff; orchestration uses live session messaging and logs.

evidence.title: guards
evidence.locator: ALL; mode; waits; reported; agentcli/talk_args.rs, codex_wire.rs, acp_wire.rs
evidence.finding: Stop, force-stop and send-draft policies are person-controlled; full access bypasses some confirmations, force-stop asks by default. Harness permission protocols supply command/tool enforcement.

evidence.title: remote
evidence.finding: Opt-in Remote pairs devices after local confirmation, assigns device capabilities and drops connections on revocation. Remote MCP exposes only projects, board, card, sessions and waiting.

evidence.title: checkout
evidence.finding: Card-specific Git worktrees and branches are made on demand. Preparation copies/links declared local files, shares environment and runs once with bounded command time. Ordinary processes run on the host, not inside a worktree security sandbox.

evidence.title: runtime
evidence.finding: Command steps stream output, enforce optional timeout and stop process groups. Cancellation is distinct from failure. Claude chat passes max-budget-usd; backend-specific limits are not universal.

evidence.title: cost
evidence.finding: Transcript-based daily/model/project/card accounting is cached by file size/mtime. Claude reported costs and known-price estimates are distinguished; not every ACP harness reports cost/context.

evidence.title: gate
evidence.locator: gating; read; unreviewed_since; stopped; completion guard
evidence.finding: Enabled completion gates read fresh evidence, review HEAD, acceptance proofs and configured stages. Failing gates block finish-card. Stop hooks eventually warn after a bounded streak; ordinary Git/deploy commands are not globally intercepted.

evidence.title: engine
evidence.locator: checked; said; evidence.rs run_check/reuse/locked; fresh.rs; config.rs
evidence.finding: Devflow requires configured check evidence after code changes, per-criterion proof and no blocking review. Named locks serialize checks and fresh green results can be reused. Stop hook cap defaults to eight.

evidence.title: sandbox
evidence.locator: Sandbox; KEPT; run preparation; bwrap/docker argv
evidence.finding: Devflow exploit tests use isolated temporary worktrees, read-only dependencies/caches, filtered environment, disabled external network and time/CPU/memory bounds. This applies to attack tests, not all coding agents.

evidence.title: review
evidence.finding: Reviews pin base/head, retain full findings and logs as project artifacts, annotate card diffs and mark stale findings against HEAD. Human false-positive decisions can edit findings.

evidence.title: publish
evidence.finding: Review publishing previews a draft and posts to a GitHub PR through the users gh login; other destination drafts require pasting. This is review publishing, not general bidirectional tracker sync.

evidence.title: git
evidence.finding: Git status/diffs/index/branches/worktrees are integrated. Landed checks ancestry and conservatively leaves squash-merged branches unlanded. No deployment rollback service follows from local Git state.
